newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-RUSSIANS AND ISRAELIS BOTH FACE MOMENT OF TRUTH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RUSSIANS AND ISRAELIS BOTH FACE MOMENT OF TRUTH.

text.p: Group five leaders Israel are in to Moscow to face their toughest test so far on Sunday, trying to take at least a point from their World Cup qualifier against a Russian side determined to make amends for past shortcomings.

The Israelis lead by two points over Russia, with whom they drew 1-1 in Tel Aviv last year, but the Russians have a game in hand. With Bulgaria close behind in third place, defeat for either side would make qualification for France problematic.

For the Israelis, whose strong start gave them probably their best chance of reaching the finals since they went to Mexico in 1970, the task in Moscow is complicated because they arrived on Thursday short-handed.

Head coach Shlomo Scharf has dropped three players, Avishai Janno, Assi Domb and Ronen Harazi, from the side that beat Cyprus 2-0 in April, while former team captain, Nir Klinger, recently announced his retirement from the national team.

The Russians, lambasted at home after dropping two points in Cyprus two months ago, also go into what could be their most important game of the season without several key players due to injury and a continued niggling problem with morale.

As well as Spartak Moscow's Ilya Tsymbalar, the serie A trio of Andrei Kanchelskis, Igor Kolyvanov and Omari Tetradze are all injured and unavailable, while two of Russia's Spanish legionnaires, Valery Karpin and Alexander Mostovoi, were dropped after internal squabbles.

Boris Ignatyev, Russia's third coach in as many years who was brought in after rancorous failures in Euro 96 and the 1994 World Cup, has continued the tradition of criticising foreign-based players for lacking commitment.
Karpin, a moody Valencia midfielder, said he would never play for Russia again after Ignatyev dropped him from the team that beat Luxembourg 3-0 in Moscow in April.
Team captain Viktor Onopko of Oviedo spoke out this week against what he said was a campaign by Russian officials against the exiles.

With so many absentees, Ignatyev will rely on home-grown talent, such as Alania Vladikavkaz's attacking midfielder Igor Yanovsky, called up at the last minute after scoring twice in his club's 3-2 win over league leaders Rotor Volgograd.
Russia - Stanislav Cherchesov; Ramiz Mamedov, Viktor Onopko, Yuri Nikiforov, Yuri Kovtun; Vladislav Radimov, Andrei Tikhonov, Dmitry Alenichev, Sergei Grishin; Igor Simutenkov, Vladimir Beschastnykh.
Israel - Rafi Cohen; Felix Halfon, Arik Bennado, Amir Shelah, Alon Harazi, David Amsalem; Avi Nimni, Haim Revivo, Eyal Berkowitz; Eli Ohana, Alon Mizrahi.
